title: Stoichiometry with gases
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:32Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: No bank point teaches using equation mole ratios to find the mass or volume of a gas: the molar volume card covers only moles-to-volume conversion, and the limiting reagents card covers ratios but not gas volumes, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: Stoichiometry with gases
card: The coefficients in a balanced equation give the mole ratio of the substances. In 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O, 2 mol of H2 reacts with 1 mol of O2.
To find an unknown, first change the given quantity to moles. Use n = m ÷ M for a mass, where M is molar mass.
Then use the mole ratio to find the moles of the substance you want.
Last, change moles to the quantity asked for. For a mass, use m = n × M. For a gas volume at SLC, use V = n × 24.8 L, as 1 mol of any gas takes up 24.8 L at SLC.
draft.remember: Go from the given quantity to moles, use the mole ratio, then convert to the answer asked for.

a.q: In 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O, how many moles of O2 react with 6.0 mol of H2?
a.why: The ratio of H2 to O2 is 2 to 1, so 6.0 mol of H2 needs 3.0 mol of O2. Using 6.0 mol ignores the ratio.
a.clue: Look at the coefficients in front of H2 and O2.

b.q: Magnesium reacts with acid: Mg + 2HCl → MgCl2 + H2. What volume of H2 at SLC forms from 0.10 mol of Mg?
b.why: The ratio of Mg to H2 is 1 to 1, so 0.10 mol of H2 forms. V = 0.10 × 24.8 = 2.48 L. Forgetting to multiply by the moles gives 24.8 L.
b.clue: Find the moles of H2 first, then change to volume.
